subsection: H. Directors and Officers Liability (D&O) Insurance
text: [3:665] Claims-made coverage: D&O policies are generally written on a “claims-made” basis—i.e., they cover claims first made against the insured director or officer during the term of the policy. A claim is “made” when the insured officer or director receives it or learns of it (see ¶ 3:294). Some policies also require the insured to report the claim to the insurer within the policy period (so-called “claims made and reported” coverage). A threshold issue in the employment context is whether the employee has taken action that constitutes a “claim.” The filing and service of a civil action would qualify as a claim under virtually any claims-made policy. However, events preceding filing suit must also be evaluated as potential claims. In the employment context, this may include such events as: — a disgruntled employee's threat of litigation; — the filing of an EEOC or FEHA “charge”; — the institution of an EEOC accusation. (1) [3:666] Where policy defines “claim”: If the policy contains a definition of “claim,” that definition controls.
